lessons.title: SAT Math Beginner Lesson 1: Linear Equations in One Variable

learningSlides.title: What is a linear equation?
learningSlides.content: A linear equation in one variable is an equation such as 3x + 5 = 20 where the variable has power 1. The main goal is to isolate the variable and keep both sides balanced.

learningSlides.title: Use inverse operations
learningSlides.content: Undo addition or subtraction first, then undo multiplication or division. For example, 3x + 5 = 20 becomes 3x = 15 and then x = 5.

learningSlides.title: Variables on both sides
learningSlides.content: Move variable terms to one side and constants to the other. In 5x - 7 = 2x + 8, subtract 2x from both sides and add 7 to both sides to get 3x = 15, so x = 5.

learningSlides.title: Special SAT idea
learningSlides.content: Some SAT questions ask whether an equation has one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions. If the variable disappears and the statement is always true, there are infinitely many solutions. If it becomes false, there is no solution.

learningSlides.title: Quick check for the presentation
learningSlides.content: Students can finish this lesson by solving one-step, two-step, and variable-on-both-sides equations and by checking the solution in the original equation.
